details: U.S. stock markets, including the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq, saw declines on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. The S&P 500 fell 0.7%, the Dow dipped 0.2%, and the Nasdaq sank 1.3%. This downturn was primarily driven by surging oil prices amid renewed Middle East tensions and rising Treasury yields, with the 30-year yield reaching its highest level since 2007. Chip stocks, in particular, experienced significant losses.
title: US Stocks Fall as Treasury Yields Rise Amid Geopolitical Tensions

details: European Central Bank chief economist Philip Lane stated on Tuesday, August 18, 2026, that Eurozone inflation at 3% is still "too high." He emphasized that despite appearing modest compared to earlier double-digit rates, this level is one percentage point above the ECB's 2% target, signifying a notable deviation that necessitates continued focus on bringing it down.
title: ECB Chief Economist Warns Eurozone Inflation Remains Too High

details: Investors are closely anticipating the release of the Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, seeking greater insight into the central bank's future stance on interest rates. The market has lowered expectations for a rate hike in September to 59%, down from 82% post-July meeting, following recent softer inflation data. The minutes are crucial given the Fed's new limited communication approach.
title: Investors Await Fed Minutes for Interest Rate Outlook Clarity

details: Bitcoin saw a 2.3% rebound to $64,282 on Tuesday, August 18, 2026, reversing some of last week's losses. This recovery was spurred by the anticipation of a White House meeting focused on cryptocurrency innovation, involving President Trump and industry leaders. However, the cryptocurrency also experienced significant outflows of $390 million from Bitcoin ETFs, marking the largest outflows since early July.
title: Bitcoin Rebounds Amid Anticipation of White House Crypto Talks
